-80.29410,36.08810.name: Wake Forest University Center for Reproductive Medicine
-80.29410,36.08810.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Jeffrey L. Deaton, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-2.14714,52.56481.name: St Jude's Women's Hospital
-2.14714,52.56481.state: 263, Penn Road, Penn, Wolverhampton, West Midlands, WV4 5SF, United Kingdom
-2.14714,52.56481.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-80.54524,43.47020.name: University of Waterloo
-80.54524,43.47020.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, December 2025
-80.54524,43.47020.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, December 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-57.57590,-25.26370.name: SENAVE — seed and plant health service
-57.57590,-25.26370.desc: Paraguay's seed authority. Engineered soy arrived in Paraguay across the border and was widely planted before it was legal, and the authority's task became regularising a situation rather than deciding one. That sequence — adoption first, approval afterwards — has happened in several countries and is rarely described in accounts of how these crops spread.

-57.57590,-25.26370.name: INBIO — Instituto de Biotecnología Agrícola
-57.57590,-25.26370.desc: Paraguay's agricultural biotechnology institute, funded by the grain trade rather than by the state, running soybean breeding jointly with the public institute IPTA and commissioning the studies that are cited back at the regulator. Its 2022 volume on engineered crops in Paraguayan agriculture was produced with the Buenos Aires Grain Exchange and an agricultural-negotiations foundation. Paraguay approved drought-tolerant HB4 wheat on the strength of this apparatus. An institute that breeds the varieties, measures their effects and publishes the measurement is doing three jobs that are ordinarily kept apart, and nothing conceals it — the arrangement is stated openly.
